_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for EIH Ltd (Oberoi group; consolidated, Rs crore). EIH reports one segment (hotels, incl. Oberoi Flight Services); we forecast it stream by stream (rooms, F&B incl. flight catering, other services; businessLines.hotel, checked against the segment in EIHOTEL.ctx.js). Operating EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116 and excludes other income (the company's own 'EBITDA' includes it). Share of associates and JVs (EIH Associated Hotels 36.81%, Avis India Mobility 40%, Oberoi Mauritius, La Roseraie de l'Atlas) sits in other income, as on Screener; minorities have no engine line and sit in the tax rate (see _taxWhy) and in the SOTP.

segments.name: Hotels (incl. flight catering)
segments._why: Sum of the three streams in businessLines.hotel. Rooms +13% / +12% / +14%: owned-hotel RevPAR +14% in Q1FY27 (Rs14,972 vs Rs13,082) and the industry +11-13% (HVS Anarock, Jul-2026), 'business on books for Q2 very positive' (12-Aug-2026 call), Rajgarh (opened Nov-2025) ramping over ~3 years; held back by renovations at Trident Nariman Point, The Oberoi Mumbai, Bengaluru and BKC (finished by October), Trident Jaipur and The Oberoi Grand Kolkata closed (Grand reopens ~Sep-2028, 197 keys) and Wildflower Hall run only on an interim operating arrangement. FY29 +14% with the Grand back and Goa/London nearer. F&B +10% / +10% / +11%: hotel F&B +6-7% in Q1 (call), flight catering (OFS Rs154 cr in Q1, 'very healthy growth'). Other services +12% / +10% / +10% (FY26 +15%).
segments._marginWhy: Operating EBITDA margin FY24 36.9%, FY25 37.5%, FY26 34.8% (OFS mix with a higher airport levy: Rs71 cr vs Rs44 cr; a Rs30 cr political donation and Rs14 cr of CSR inside other expenses; higher repairs), Q1FY27 25.4% vs 27.9% (Rajgarh ramp-up, Rs4 cr extra marketing, Rs7.5 cr renovation write-offs, fuel costs; like-for-like ex-Rajgarh margin 30.6% on the company's measure). 35.0% / 35.8% / 36.5%: rate-led operating leverage and no repeat of the donation, against labour-code wage costs, Rajgarh and the Grand's pre-opening costs.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in the segment
_unallocWhy: Single reported segment: the segment is consolidated operating EBITDA.

businessLines._why: FY26 base (AR FY26 consolidated note 30, Rs cr): rooms 1,410.5, food & beverage 1,095.6 (incl. flight catering), other services 433.5 = 2,939.6. Growth per stream in segments[0]._why.

_capexWhy: FY26 Rs680 cr on the company's measure (Rs330 cr to convert the Mumbai hotel land from leasehold to freehold, ~Rs125 cr Rajgarh, ~Rs100 cr renovations, the rest replacement). CFO: 'we'll keep spending in that range [Rs600-700 cr] in the next one or two years ... it will go up higher towards FY29-30' (29-May-2026 call); CARE (Dec-2025): ~Rs500-600 cr a year. Rs650 / 700 / 800 cr: Grand Kolkata, Goa, London, Tirupati, Gandikota, then Hebbal (120 + 300 keys and ~7.6 lakh sq ft of commercial space).
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs143 cr = ~3.5% of average gross block (Rs4,096 cr; AR ten-year table Rs3,737 cr -> Rs4,455 cr); Q1FY27 Rs37 cr (Rs148 cr annualised). 3.0% on the model's gross block (Screener Rs4,679 cr incl. right-of-use and intangibles) gives ~Rs150 cr in FY27E, rising with capex.
_treasuryWhy: Zero: the engine would apply it to net cash after lease liabilities and strategic stakes; treasury income is built in otherIncome.
_otherIncomeWhy: Screener basis (other income incl. share of associates, before exceptional items): FY25 Rs195 cr, FY26 Rs222 cr = company other income Rs166 cr + associates and JVs Rs57 cr. Built: treasury ~6.5% on ~Rs1,450 cr average surplus funds (Rs1,335 cr Mar-26, Rs1,368 cr Jun-26) = ~Rs95 cr (FY26 interest Rs81 cr + fund gains Rs16 cr); rent from investment property ~Rs30 cr (FY26 Rs29 cr); shared services and miscellaneous ~Rs20 cr (FY26 Rs23 cr; we drop the Rs16 cr of write-backs); associates and JVs ~Rs55 cr (FY25 Rs59 cr, FY26 Rs57 cr, Q1FY27 Rs4 cr in the weak quarter) = Rs200 cr. Then +Rs15 cr a year as cash builds and EIH Associated Hotels opens Visakhapatnam (2027).
_interestWhy: No bank debt since FY24 (AR ten-year table). FY26 finance cost Rs23 cr, of which lease interest Rs21 cr (AR note 34); Q1FY27 Rs5 cr.
_taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: no minority line). FY25: tax ~25% of PBT before exceptional items plus minorities ~3% = 28%; FY26: tax was higher (Q4 32%; 'PAT was down due to the tax impact'), leakage ~33%; Q1FY27: tax Rs49 cr + minorities Rs3 cr on PBT Rs169 cr = 30.8%. 30%: tax ~26-27% (associates' profit is post-tax) plus minorities ~3% (Svara 40%, Oberoi Kerala 20%, Indonesian partners).
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs1.50 a share (FY25 Rs1.20, FY24 Rs1.10) = 15% of consolidated EPS (Rs10.05). 15%.

dcf._betaWhy: No bank debt and net cash, so the 12.2% cost of equity is the discount rate; beta 0.95, as for IHCL and ITC Hotels: travel demand is cyclical (Covid, the 2026 West Asia shock), no financial leverage.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian luxury travel grows with nominal GDP; 6% nominal, the top of the house range (IHCL, ITC Hotels).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~12% to 8% by year 15 as the owned pipeline opens and rate growth normalises.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 36%: near FY29E; EIH earned 37-38% in FY24-25 before the flight-catering mix shift.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades from ~20% of revenue (FY29E, Hebbal and the owned pipeline) to 12%: EIH grows mainly by owning (825 owned keys in the pipeline vs 1,833 managed), renovation ~5% plus growth keys.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Foreign arrivals return by H2FY27, owned RevPAR grows ~14-15% a year, Rajgarh and the Grand ramp fast, EIH keeps Wildflower Hall on a long contract and the market pays the top quartile of EIH's own post-Covid multiple range after the same sector move.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The 2026 travel shock lingers (Oberoi hotels depend more on foreign guests), RevPAR grows ~6-7%, Wildflower Hall is lost, project delays (Grand, Gandikota, Goa) continue, labour-code wage costs stick and the multiple stays at the bottom quartile after the sector de-rating.

parts.note: Svara Hotels 40%, Oberoi Kerala 20%, PT Widja Putra Karya 30%, PT Waka Oberoi 10%, PT Astina Graha Ubud 40% (AR FY26 note 48). Checked in EIHOTEL.ctx2.js.

parts.note: Listed associate that owns Trident hotels managed by EIH (incl. Jaipur; Visakhapatnam from 2027); bull 10%, bear 30% discount (house rule for listed stakes).

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-28E (model: cash and investments less lease liabilities)
parts.note: Mar-26 on Screener: cash and investments less borrowings (all lease liabilities). Other JVs (Avis India 40%, Oberoi Mauritius, La Roseraie) stay at book.

methods.name: Sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA)
methods.why: How the street values hotel companies and has valued EIH: EV/EBITDA on two-year-forward EBITDA (ICICI Securities and ICICI Direct 2022-23; Axis Capital initiated Buy on 29-Sep-2026, method not public). Sep-28E EBITDA, less minorities, the listed associate at market less 20%, plus net cash.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on attributable earnings: own forward P/E median since Apr-2022 adjusted for the hotel peers' P/E move over the same windows.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, 12.2% discount rate, 6% terminal growth, plus net cash.
